findings.label: Thick-walled cavity on chest imaging
findings.evidence: large (9.3 × 9.6 cm), thick-walled cavitary lesion with peripheral enhancement

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial contrast-enhanced CT shows a large thick-walled left lower lobe cavitary lesion with an air-fluid level, consistent with primary lung abscess as stated in the caption and in-text. B: Coronal contrast-enhanced CT demonstrates the same large thick-walled left lower lobe cavitary lesion, supporting the diagnosis of primary lung abscess.
panels.attribution_text: Al Hariri et al. A Large Community-Acquired Lung Abscess Caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenges.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.105657. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced CT thorax. Axial (A) and coronal (B) contrast-enhanced CT images of the chest definitively characterize the left lower lobe abscess. The images demonstrate a large (9.3 × 9.6 cm), thick-walled cavitary lesion with peripheral enhancement (arrows), confirming the diagnosis of a primary lung abscess and excluding pleural involvement.
in_text_mentions: Contrast-enhanced CT of the thorax definitively characterized a 9.3 × 9.6 cm, thick-walled, peripherally enhancing cavitary mass in the posterior segment of the left lower lobe, consistent with a primary lung abscess (Figures 2A-2B). The study incidentally noted multiple calcified gallstones without acute pathology.

panels.rationale: The image is a chest radiograph of an adolescent patient diagnosed with an Enterococcus faecalis-associated lung abscess. The radiograph clearly shows an opacity in the posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe, which is consistent with the radiological presentation of the target disease.
panels.attribution_text: Mendes et al. Enterococcus faecalis-associated lung abscess in a male adolescent- a case report.. BMC pediatrics 2020. doi:10.1186/s12887-020-2003-8. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Chest x-ray performed on his first emergency department visit
in_text_mentions: at his first visit to the emergency department, he was afebrile, with no signs of respiratory distress, but with diminished breath sounds on the left side. He complained of pain on palpation of the left lower costal margin. A left costal grid and a chest x-ray was performed (Fig. 1), which showed the same opacity on the posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe and no signs of rib fracture; thus, the patient was discharged with oral amoxicillin 1000 mg three times a day with the diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia.
